passages.text: Supervised learning trains a model from examples paired with labels. The model learns a mapping from input features to a known target.
Unsupervised learning works with data that has no supplied target labels. It can group similar examples or discover structure in the data.
In reinforcement learning, an agent interacts with an environment, takes actions, and receives rewards or penalties. It learns a policy that aims to maximize long-term reward.
Overfitting occurs when a model fits peculiarities of its training examples and performs poorly on new data. A large gap between training and validation performance can be a warning sign.
Split data into training, validation, and test sets. Use training data to fit model parameters, validation data to compare choices, and keep the test set for a final evaluation.
Gradient descent updates model parameters in the direction that reduces the loss. A learning rate controls the size of each update.
Classification predicts a discrete class or category, such as whether an email is spam or not spam.
Regression predicts a numeric continuous value, such as a temperature or a house price.
Precision is true positives divided by all predicted positives. Recall is true positives divided by all actual positives. F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
A neural network is made of layers of units that transform input values. During training, parameters are adjusted to reduce a loss function.
A Python list is an ordered, mutable collection. It can contain duplicate values, and elements can be accessed by position.
A Python dictionary stores key-value pairs. Keys are unique within a dictionary and are used to retrieve their associated values.
A Python tuple is an ordered collection that is generally immutable after creation. Lists are mutable, while tuples are not normally changed in place.
In standard CPython builds, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) allows only one thread at a time to execute Python bytecode in a process. Threads can still help with I/O-bound work.
Python async and await provide cooperative concurrency. An event loop switches between tasks when a task awaits an operation, which is useful for many I/O-bound operations.
Image thresholding compares each pixel with a threshold value. In simple binary thresholding, pixels on one side become zero and pixels on the other side become the maximum value.
A convolution applies a small kernel across an image. The weighted neighborhood calculation can detect patterns such as edges or blur the image.
Morphological image operations use a structuring element to change shapes in a binary image. Erosion shrinks foreground regions and dilation expands them.
HSV represents color using hue, saturation, and value. Separating these components can make some color-based image processing tasks easier than working directly with RGB values.
The Domain Name System (DNS) looks up records that map domain names to information such as IP addresses. A resolver may use cached answers before contacting other DNS servers.
HTTP is an application-layer protocol used for requests and responses between clients and servers. HTTP methods such as GET and POST communicate the intended operation.
TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between applications. It uses acknowledgements and retransmission to handle packet loss.
TLS protects data exchanged over a connection using encryption and integrity checks. HTTPS uses TLS to protect HTTP communication.
Active recall is a study practice in which a learner tries to retrieve information from memory instead of only rereading it.
Spaced repetition schedules review across increasing intervals. It aims to revisit material over time rather than concentrate every review in one session.
Use a validation set to compare models and tune hyperparameters. Reserve the test set for a final evaluation after model choices are complete.
This note recommends checking the test set repeatedly during training and using its score to tune model hyperparameters.
